fieldMarks: Smallest eider, 43-47 cm, square-headed; often floats with tail cocked up
Breeding male: peachy chest, black neck ring and eye spot, green and black crest knob
Female: plain dark brown, can suggest a female scoter or dabbling duck; note the square head and white-bordered blue wing patch
Wing patch (speculum) is iridescent blue-purple with white borders in all ages
behavior: Sociable; flies in tightly packed flocks and feeds in compact groups, dives together
Lone birds may join flocks of harlequin ducks or other divers
Winter diet mostly mollusks and crustaceans; tundra diet mostly aquatic insects
Male has a weak moan; female low growling notes
habitat: Nests on low tundra near lakes and ponds, often inland; winters at sea near rocky shores or pack-ice edges.
range: Breeds in Arctic Russia and in Alaska (Arctic Coastal Plain and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta); Alaska and eastern Siberian birds molt and winter mainly along the Alaska Peninsula; some Russian-Atlantic birds winter in Europe.

lookalikes.name: Female scoters
lookalikes.howToTell: Steller's female has a square head and white-bordered blue wing patch.

lookalikes.name: Harlequin duck
lookalikes.howToTell: Steller's eider associates with harlequin flocks; identify by the wing patch and head shape.
